dedupe_keys.name: hawaii statewide coastal highway program data cresi ocean hazards database and hazard map series

description: The State of Hawaii Statewide Coastal Highway Program Report (2019) is backed by a family of datasets on Mendeley Data from the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, funded by the Hawaii Department of Transportation. The Coastal Road Exposure Susceptibility Index (CRESI) dataset contains measures, interpretations and rankings for 303 mileposts and points of interest along coastal state routes, from variables such as coastal geomorphology, erodible land buffer, slope, ground cover and structures, road base, armouring, relative sea-level change, shoreline change, tides and wave height, with Access databases and field forms by island. The Ocean Hazards Database (OHD) ranks 302 mileposts on sea-level rise, waves, projected shoreline change, armouring, tsunami flow depth, storm surge and nearshore habitat, with GIS map packages; further map series cover sea-level rise, tsunami and storm surge inundation, waves, shoreline change and offshore transects, and LiDAR-based digital elevation models by island. Coverage is regional (Hawaii). The data are free under CC BY 4.0 and available to download from Mendeley Data. Caveats: the indices use the report's own ranking criteria, and the data date from 2019. They support hazard exposure and climate adaptation planning for coastal highways. They complement the NOAA sea level rise data and are related to the FHWA resilience case studies.
